data.title: Contango ORE Earnings Call Signals Stronger 2027
data.description:
Contango ORE ((CTGO)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Contango ORE’s earnings call struck a cautiously optimistic tone despite a difficult 2026. Management highlighted a quarterly loss, higher costs and weather disruptions, but said Manh Choh remains cash-flow positive and emphasized stronger production, debt repayment and project progress ahead.

No Planned Financing or Dilution

Management firmly rejected suggestions that it is pursuing a $75 million financing or equity raise. The shelf registration and at-the-market facility are flexibility tools for possible opportunities, not commitments to issue shares, and management said there is no current need to dilute investors.

Cash Flow Supports Debt Repayment

Contango ended the quarter with $56.6 million in cash and expected about $6 million from a post-quarter distribution. Expected quarterly distributions of $22 million to $24 million, combined with 2027 cash flow, are intended to repay approximately $15 million due in March and $30 million due in June.

Debt and Hedges Nearing an End

Management described removing the company’s hedges as the first step toward a cleaner balance sheet. Once the March and June debt maturities are repaid, Contango expects to be both hedge-free and debt-free, although it does not plan to buy back shares while debt remains outstanding.

2026 Hit by Low Production and Weather

The company reported a quarterly net loss of $23 million, including $27 million of exploration spending that accounting rules require it to expense. Cash costs were about $2,700 per ounce, above prior guidance of roughly $2,000, as diesel, consumables and lower production weighed on results.

Heavy Rains Disrupted Processing

Manh Choh mined and transported about 300,000 tonnes of ore but processed only 200,000 tonnes during the quarter after heavy September rains. Management said the mismatch inflated third-quarter costs, while the unprocessed ore should provide a benefit in the fourth quarter.

South Pit Offers a Better Production Profile

The South pit contains more tonnes and higher grades than the North pit, but it also has more sulfide ore, sulfur and copper. As mining moves beyond waste removal and pre-stripping, management expects higher grades and significantly more production, although consumables and diesel costs will remain a pressure point.

Johnson Tract Clears a Legal Hurdle

A federal court dismissed all three challenges to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ Section 404 permit for Johnson Tract. The ruling allows Contango to proceed toward tunnel construction, while management acknowledged that further litigation and permitting work could still affect timing.

Johnson Tract Site Work Advances

Contractors completed the road linking the camp with the proposed portal and finished additional camp and portal construction originally planned for a later period. The progress reduces some early execution risk as the company continues evaluating how the project will be developed and processed.

Exploration Exceeded Plans at Kitsault

Contango drilled 56,000 meters at Kitsault, well above the 40,000 meters originally planned, while staying within the same budget. The added work is expected to improve the project’s resource estimate by incorporating drilling, geotechnical, hydrology and metallurgy information.

Kitsault Milestones Remain Ahead

The company expects a Kitsault Mineral Resource Estimate by the end of the first quarter, with higher total tonnage and more silver, gold and base metals expected. An initial assessment is planned for the fourth quarter of 2027, and management characterized Kitsault as a silver deposit whose value is primarily tied to gold, with about 10% from copper, lead and zinc.

Lucky Shot Keeps Moving Toward Development

Lucky Shot remains in full-scale drilling, including work from a second underground rig, with a resource estimate targeted for the end of the second quarter. Management is also targeting a feasibility study by year-end, a resource of 400,000 to 500,000 ounces and production around the end of 2028.

Lucky Shot Could Be a Fast, Modest-Cost Build

Management said the remaining cost to bring Lucky Shot into production is estimated at $50 million to $60 million. The project’s larger-than-expected mineralized system includes veins such as KM and CK, and could move from a production decision to operations in months rather than years.

A Three-Project Growth Portfolio

Contango has invested roughly $75 million across Lucky Shot, Kitsault Valley and Johnson Tract to reduce development risk. Management sees a path from current production of about 60,000 gold ounces toward 200,000 gold ounces and 5 million silver ounces, supported by high-grade, lower-cost deposits and direct-shipping potential.

Winter Spending Should Ease

Exploration spending is expected to slow during the final quarter of the year. Kitsault is largely shut down except for technical work, Johnson Tract is on low-cost care and maintenance, and Lucky Shot remains active through approximately March.

Processing Choices Are Still Open

Contango is evaluating two processing options for Johnson Tract and Kitsault under confidentiality agreements. A decision is expected next year, while management said any potential acquisition would likely be limited to processing-related opportunities rather than a change in focus from its existing portfolio.

Market Reaction Reflected Confusion

Contango’s shares fell nearly 10% on twice-normal volume after the results, and the stock weakened again during the call. Management attributed part of the decline to inaccurate AI-generated summaries that portrayed the shelf and ATM facility as a $75 million financing.

Forward Guidance Points to a Stronger 2027

Management expects 2027 production to be significantly higher than in 2026, with total costs relatively flat and sulfide recovery around 85%; third-quarter recovery reached 86.5%. Earlier production ranges of roughly 70,000 to 80,000 ounces may be reduced after mine-plan changes, while cash costs could fall from 2026 levels toward roughly $1,600 to $2,000 per ounce, with formal guidance expected within about a month.

Contango’s call presented 2026 as a temporary trough rather than a change in strategy. Higher 2027 output, lower unit costs, debt repayment, cleaner financial statements and progress at three development projects support management’s bullish outlook, though commodity prices, permitting, litigation and processing decisions remain important risks.

data.title: Palatin Technologies Earnings Call Highlights MC4R Progress, Cash Strain
data.description:
Palatin Technologies, Inc. ((PTN)) has held its Q1 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

The call struck an optimistic tone as Palatin Technologies highlighted progress across its MC4R obesity pipeline, encouraging preclinical findings and rising industry interest. That confidence was tempered by a steep revenue decline, a $5.1 million net loss, higher cash use and just $3.7 million in cash, making new financing an important near-term issue.

MC4R Programs Move Toward 2027 Milestones

Palatin is advancing next-generation MC4R obesity therapies toward several development milestones. The lead lipidated peptide is targeted to enter Phase I in the first half of 2027, while initial data are expected in the second half; the oral small-molecule program is planned for clinical entry later in 2027.

Lead Peptide Shows Weight-Loss Potential

In diet-induced obese mice, PL2000 produced significant reductions in food intake and body weight after once-weekly subcutaneous dosing. Pharmacokinetic results in larger animals also supported the possibility of weekly or less frequent dosing in humans, although clinical testing is still required.

Selectivity Could Address Hyperpigmentation

Compounds from Palatin’s two next-generation peptide series showed potent MC4R activity without agonizing MC1R in testing. Management said this profile could substantially reduce or eliminate MC1R-related hyperpigmentation, but the benefit remains unconfirmed until human studies are completed.

Toxicology and Manufacturing Stay on Track

Most in vitro toxicology work for the lead peptide has been completed, and 28-day rat and dog studies are next. Those studies are the main gating item for filing, while manufacturing documentation, drug-product work and stability testing remain targeted for completion in the second quarter of 2027.

Oral Small-Molecule Candidates Improve

Palatin has identified oral small-molecule candidates with stronger potency and MC4R selectivity than earlier programs, along with favorable preclinical bioavailability. Further optimization is focused on potency, receptor selectivity, gastrointestinal tolerability and suitability for long-term use.

Oral Peptide Work Adds Another Option

The company has developed selective MC4R peptide agonists that show gastrointestinal stability and oral bioavailability, supporting additional development. Palatin said lipidated peptides may be suitable for oral delivery because absorbed compounds bind to albumin and can remain in the body longer.

Portfolio Offers Multiple Development Paths

Palatin is continuing work on its non-lipidated PL1000 peptide series, including formulations designed for extended dosing. Alongside that effort, it is pursuing lipidated injectable peptides, oral small molecules and oral peptides, aiming to reduce dependence on any single compound or delivery method.

MC4R Investment Rises Sharply

Research and development expense increased about 36% to roughly $3.4 million from $2.5 million. Spending directly tied to MC4R obesity programs more than doubled to approximately $2.1 million, reflecting toxicology, long-acting peptide work and oral small-molecule optimization.

Partnerships Could Support Portfolio Value

The Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration provides research reimbursement and potential milestone payments and royalties. Palatin also transferred future development responsibility for dry-eye asset PL9643 to Altanispac Labs while retaining possible future economics, and it is reviewing partners for other assets.

Boehringer Program Continues to Advance

Management said the Boehringer Ingelheim program is progressing well and has generated approximately $10 million for Palatin since August 2025. Additional milestones may follow as development advances, although the company did not disclose their expected timing or value.

External Interest in MC4R Is Growing

Palatin cited rising interest in the MC4R pathway from specialty and large pharmaceutical companies, including AstraZeneca, Gilead and PepGen. Management said more companies are approaching Palatin, viewing the attention as validation of both the mechanism and the potential market.

Experience Supports the MC4R Strategy

Palatin pointed to more than 25 years of operating history and experience with the melanocortin receptor system. It also highlighted prior bremelanotide development, proprietary medicinal chemistry and pharmacology expertise, and peptide-lipidation capabilities as competitive strengths.

Cardiovascular Safety Will Be Studied

The company plans to examine blood pressure and heart-rhythm effects during its toxicology program using dedicated studies, ECG monitoring and short- and longer-term testing. Appropriate blood-pressure assessments are also planned for clinical studies, reflecting the importance of cardiovascular safety in obesity treatments.

Revenue Falls After Prior Milestone Payments

Fiscal first-quarter collaboration and license revenue plunged about 96% to approximately $362,000 from $8.8 million a year earlier. The prior-year figure included substantial upfront Boehringer milestone payments, while the latest quarter mainly reflected research and development service revenue.

Net Loss Widens With Development Spending

Palatin reported a fiscal first-quarter net loss of about $5.1 million, or $1.29 per basic and diluted share. General and administrative expense rose 24% to approximately $2.1 million, largely because of higher stock-based compensation and professional fees.

Operating Cash Use Accelerates

Net cash used in operating activities climbed about 131% to approximately $3.7 million from $1.6 million in the comparable period. Palatin had approximately $3.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, 2026, underscoring its limited financial flexibility.

Additional Capital Will Be Needed

Management said advancing the pipeline through the next stages of clinical development will require additional capital. Palatin is considering public or private equity, strategic collaborations and other financing options, but offered no assurance on the timing or terms of a transaction.

Clinical Benefits Remain Unproven

Although the company expects its selectivity profile to reduce or avoid pigmentation, it acknowledged that animal models do not reliably predict this effect. The planned Phase I trial will assess the lead peptide’s safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and pigmentation profile.

Oral Programs Trail the Lead Peptide

Management said the oral small-molecule and oral peptide programs are tracking roughly two quarters behind the lipidated peptide. Oral clinical initiation is expected in the second half of 2027, with initial data targeted for the first half of 2028.

Forward Guidance Centers on 2027 Clinical Entry

Palatin is targeting a Phase I single-dose, multiple-dose and multiple-ascending-dose study for its lead lipidated peptide in the first half of 2027, with initial data in the second half. The 28-day rat and dog studies are the filing gate, while oral small-molecule candidate selection and IND-enabling work are planned for the first half of 2027.

Outlook Calls for Higher Spending and Financing

The company expects development costs to rise as manufacturing, toxicology, regulatory work and clinical preparation expand. Oral programs are expected to deliver data in the first half of 2028, while Palatin continues pursuing financing and strategic partnerships to support its plans.

Palatin’s earnings call presented a promising development story built around selective MC4R therapies, several delivery strategies and growing partner interest. However, the sharp revenue drop, widening loss, rising cash burn and need for new capital remain substantial risks as the company works toward its 2027 clinical goals.

data.title: Kyntra Bio Earnings Call Highlights Roxadustat Pivot
data.description:
Kyntra Bio, Inc. ((KYNB)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Kyntra Bio’s Roxadustat Strategy Offers Cautious Hope After Pipeline Setback

The earnings call carried a cautiously positive tone as Kyntra Bio shifted its focus to roxadustat after ending the FG-3246 and FG-3180 program. Strong post-hoc MATTERHORN results, FDA alignment and improved financing were encouraging, although safety concerns, limited subgroup size and the need for additional funding remain important risks.

Roxadustat Becomes the Core Strategy

Kyntra Bio said it is becoming a pure-play rare disease company focused on phase III development of roxadustat for anemia in lower-risk MDS patients with high transfusion needs. The planned study is targeted to start in the first quarter of 2027, but only after the company completes a partnership or raises outside capital.

MATTERHORN Shows Transfusion Benefits

In the high-transfusion-burden group, 36% of roxadustat patients achieved at least eight weeks of transfusion independence during the first 28 weeks, compared with 7% on placebo. Over 52 weeks, the rates were 45% and 13%, respectively, with nominal p-values of 0.041 and 0.043.

Responses Appeared Durable

Roxadustat also produced longer periods without transfusions in the high-burden population. Within 52 weeks, 36% of treated patients achieved at least 12 weeks of transfusion independence, versus 7% for placebo, while 18% reached at least 16 weeks compared with none in the placebo group.

Hemoglobin Levels Improved

Mean hemoglobin increased by about 1 gram per deciliter from baseline among roxadustat-treated patients and remained elevated through week 28. By contrast, average hemoglobin in the placebo group stayed near or slightly below baseline, supporting the drug’s effect on anemia control.

Activity Across Ring Sideroblast Groups

Roxadustat showed activity in both ring sideroblast-negative and ring sideroblast-positive patients. In the high-transfusion-burden group, eight-week transfusion independence reached 38% and 33%, respectively, while rates in the full analysis set were 48% and 46%.

Results in ESA-Refractory Patients

The drug also showed a response among patients who had failed erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. In this high-burden subgroup, 31% of roxadustat-treated patients achieved at least eight weeks of transfusion independence within 28 weeks, compared with none receiving placebo.

Efficacy Across EPO Levels

Management said roxadustat outperformed placebo on the eight-week transfusion-independence measure among patients with baseline erythropoietin levels below 200 and those above 200. The finding suggests the potential benefit may not be limited to one EPO-defined patient group.

Existing Global Experience

Roxadustat is approved in more than 40 countries for anemia linked to chronic kidney disease, and more than 1 million patients have received it since its first approval in 2019. Kyntra Bio said that experience demonstrated hemoglobin responses and significantly fewer transfusions.

Planned Phase III Design

The proposed double-blind, placebo-controlled study will randomize patients two-to-one to oral roxadustat or placebo, both alongside best supportive care. Treatment will be given three times weekly, with the primary endpoint defined as eight consecutive weeks of red blood cell transfusion independence during the first 24 weeks.

Enrollment and Study Milestones

The trial is expected to enroll 201 patients over 24 months at approximately 100 to 110 sites, although management cautioned that enrollment could take longer. The company is targeting an interim analysis in the second half of 2028 and a primary analysis in the first half of 2030.

FDA Aligns on Dosing and Eligibility

Following a Type C meeting, Kyntra Bio said the FDA was unequivocally aligned with a starting dose of 2.5 milligrams per kilogram and a maximum dose of 3.5 milligrams per kilogram. The company also tightened eligibility criteria for patients with medical histories suggesting elevated cardiovascular or thrombotic risk.

Oral Treatment Supports Commercial Case

Roxadustat is designed as an oral therapy taken three times weekly, unlike luspatercept and imetelstat, which require an injection or infusion in a medical office. Physician research identified initial adoption potential in second-line or later treatment for ring sideroblast-negative patients after an ESA or luspatercept, with possible expansion to other groups.

Large Potential MDS Market

Kyntra Bio estimates that about 74,000 people in the United States have MDS, including roughly 52,000 with lower-risk disease and 41,000 with diagnosed anemia. An external assessment by ZS Associates estimated that roxadustat could have peak U.S. sales of approximately $1 billion.

Royalty Obligation Reduced

An amended NovaQuest royalty financing agreement cut Kyntra Bio’s maximum aggregate payment obligation to $65 million from $125 million. The company made an accelerated $42.6 million payment in the third quarter, bringing total payments to $50 million and leaving a remaining obligation capped at $15 million.

Cash Runway Extends Into 2028

Kyntra Bio reported $44.1 million in cash equivalents, investments and accounts receivable as of September 30, 2026. Following the termination of the FG-3246 and FG-3180 program, management expects its cash runway to extend into 2028, although funding for the next trial remains unresolved.

Net Income Benefits From Debt Restructuring

Third-quarter 2026 net income from continuing operations was $0.2 million, or $0.04 per diluted share, compared with a $13.1 million loss, or $3.25 per share, a year earlier. The improvement was mainly driven by a $14 million gain tied to the NovaQuest debt restructuring.

Revenue Increased in the Quarter

Third-quarter total revenue rose to $1.8 million from $1.1 million in the same period of 2025. The increase provided modest top-line support as the company redirected resources toward its roxadustat development strategy.

FG-3246 and FG-3180 Program Ends

After a planned interim analysis, Kyntra Bio concluded that the phase II monotherapy study of FG-3246 and its companion PET imaging agent, FG-3180, lacked sufficient efficacy to justify continued development. The company is terminating the study, returning the asset to Fortis Therapeutics and beginning the wind-down process.

Program Missed Its Efficacy Bar

The phase II program was designed to achieve at least 10 months of median radiographic progression-free survival at final analysis. Management said the interim data did not support reaching that threshold in either the all-comers or CD46-enriched populations, while competing data had raised the clinical standard.

FG-3246 Data Remain Under Review

Kyntra Bio has not yet completed its analysis of CD46 expression data and could not say when, or in what form, the results would be disclosed. Management said the overall findings were not strong enough to support further company investment in the program.

Roxadustat Safety Remains a Concern

Grade 3-or-higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 38% of roxadustat-treated patients across MATTERHORN, compared with 21% for placebo. In the high-transfusion-burden subgroup, the gap widened to 65% for roxadustat versus 27% for placebo.

Cardiovascular Events Need Monitoring

The company also reported an imbalance in cardiovascular and thrombotic events. Eight patients experienced a significant event; six paused treatment and later restarted, while two remained on therapy as their events resolved.

Operating Expenses Rose Sharply

Third-quarter operating costs and expenses increased to $14.6 million from $6.5 million a year earlier. Research and development spending climbed to $8.3 million from $1.2 million, while selling, general and administrative expenses rose to $5.8 million from $5.3 million.

Funding Is the Main Trial Constraint

Management said operational preparation is not the main obstacle to launching the phase III study. The rate limiter is securing either a strategic partner or an external capital raise, making financing progress a key catalyst for Kyntra Bio investors.

Post-Hoc Evidence Has Limits

During the question-and-answer session, management acknowledged that the lower-risk MDS efficacy findings came from a relatively small post-hoc subgroup. It argued that the signal was supported by consistent results across high transfusion burden, ESA-refractory status, EPO levels and ring sideroblast analyses.

Guidance Points to a Funded Development Plan

Kyntra Bio expects to reduce operating expenses by more than $20 million across 2027 and 2028 and maintain cash into 2028. Subject to partnership or financing, it plans to begin the roxadustat phase III trial in the first quarter of 2027, enroll 201 patients across 100 to 110 sites, and conduct a futility-only interim analysis about 18 months after initiation.

The company expects the interim review after half of the patients complete 24 weeks or discontinue treatment, with a futility threshold below 30% conditional power. Kyntra Bio is targeting a phase III interim analysis in the second half of 2028, a primary analysis in the first half of 2030 and approximately $1 billion in peak U.S. sales.

Kyntra Bio’s call combined a major pipeline retreat with a more focused roxadustat strategy. The drug’s efficacy signals and improved royalty structure offer reasons for optimism, but safety findings, small post-hoc populations and the need to secure funding mean investors are likely to view the opportunity as promising but still high risk.

data.title: Reliance Global Group Earnings Call Highlights GPU Ambitions
data.description:
Reliance Global Group ((XGPU)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Reliance Global Group’s earnings call struck a positive but measured tone, with management highlighting the Oblivus acquisition, strong GPU demand and a stronger balance sheet. However, lower commission revenue, a deeper adjusted EBITDA loss and net income boosted by asset-sale gains showed that the company still must improve its core operating performance.

Oblivus Creates an AI Infrastructure Platform

Reliance completed its acquisition of Oblivus on November 3, adding a GPU cloud computing platform and marketplace serving AI training, inference and other demanding applications. Oblivus reported approximately $1.5 million in revenue during the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, based on unaudited records, and the deal included $3 million in cash plus potential milestone payments.

GPU Exchange Targets Rapid Capacity Expansion

Management plans to expand GPU Exchange by investing in company-owned GPU capacity, broadening its network of third-party providers and attracting new customers. The company is pursuing data center capacity and its own GPU fleet to support larger contracts over the next few quarters.

Demand for GPU Computing Remains Strong

Executives described demand for GPU cloud computing as insatiable, saying customers are actively seeking additional supply. Oblivus adds important customer and supplier relationships, along with an existing technology platform that management called extremely powerful.

Balance Sheet Strengthened

Cash rose to $6.7 million from $1.3 million at December 31, 2025, while working capital increased to $6.9 million from $1.9 million. Stockholders’ equity also climbed to $12.4 million from $6.4 million at year-end, giving Reliance more financial flexibility.

Term Debt Fully Repaid

Reliance repaid all outstanding term debt during the third quarter. The move eliminates approximately $1 million in annual principal, interest and fee payments and reduces the company’s financing burden.

Insurance Asset Sales Sharpen Operating Focus

The company completed the sales of Altruis Benefit Consulting and Southwestern Montana Insurance Center, monetizing selected insurance assets. Management said the transactions allow it to direct more resources toward GPU Exchange and other businesses with greater growth potential.

Operating Expenses and Loss Improved

Total operating expenses fell 17% to $5.3 million from $6.4 million in the year-earlier quarter, mainly because of lower share-based compensation and reduced costs from divested agencies. The operating loss narrowed to $3.5 million from $3.9 million.

Net Income Turned Positive

Reliance reported consolidated net income of $3.3 million, compared with a net loss of $1.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Basic earnings per share were $2.39, while diluted earnings per share were $2.34.

RELI Exchange Reaches All 50 States

RELI Exchange continued to grow commission revenue during the quarter and is now licensed in every U.S. state. The nationwide licensing footprint supports service to customers and partners across the country.

InsurTech GDP Expands Distribution Opportunities

Reliance established InsurTech GDP to develop commercial partnerships with businesses that want to offer insurance products to their existing customers. The company said its technology, carrier relationships, servicing capabilities and licenses can support co-branded offerings without partners building their own insurance infrastructure.

Large Insurance Partnerships Under Discussion

Management said it is in serious discussions with, and has begun relationships with, partners representing hundreds of thousands of employees. RELI Exchange remains a major focus, with systems designed to support significant growth without a comparable increase in expenses.

Profitability Remains a Core Objective

Executives said the goal is to improve underlying operations and generate profit from RELI Exchange and GPU Exchange rather than rely primarily on business-sale gains. The company is working toward reporting regular operating profits.

NASDAQ Listing and Rebranding Completed

Reliance’s common stock began trading on NASDAQ under the symbol XGPU on November 10, replacing EZRA. The company is also adopting GPU Exchange as its doing-business-as name while retaining Reliance Global Group, Inc. as its legal corporate name.

Commission Revenue Declined

Third-quarter consolidated commission revenue decreased to $1.8 million from $2.5 million in the prior-year period. The decline reflected the sale of Employee Benefits Solutions in 2025 and the 2026 divestitures of Altruis and Southwestern Montana, partly offset by RELI Exchange growth and changes at retained agencies.

Commission Expense Fell With Revenue

Commission expense declined to approximately $784,000 from $996,000 a year earlier. The reduction was consistent with the lower level of commission revenue during the quarter.

Adjusted EBITDA Loss Worsened

Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.9 million, compared with a loss of $700,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The result highlights the gap between Reliance’s growth initiatives and sustainable operating profitability.

Net Income Was Boosted by Asset Sales

The $3.3 million net profit included $7.7 million in gains from the sales of Altruis and Montana, consisting of $5.8 million and $1.9 million, respectively. Those gains were partly offset by asset and investment impairments, interest expense, a debt-extinguishment loss and other nonrecurring items.

Oblivus Was Not Yet in Third-Quarter Results

Because the Oblivus acquisition closed on November 3, its revenue and operating results were not included in Reliance’s reported third-quarter financial statements. Its contribution will therefore appear in periods following the closing date.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management plans to build GPU Exchange through company-owned capacity, third-party suppliers, data center access and new customers, with the aim of supporting large contracts in the near term. It also expects RELI Exchange and GPU Exchange to move toward regular profitability, while RELI Exchange’s nationwide licensing and scalable platform provide room for substantial expansion.

Reliance Global Group enters its next phase with a stronger balance sheet, no term debt and a major new AI infrastructure asset. Still, declining commission revenue and worsening adjusted EBITDA show that investors will be watching closely for evidence that GPU Exchange and RELI Exchange can convert growth opportunities into recurring operating profits.

data.title: Sirius Real Estate Earnings Call Signals Growth Amid Risks
data.description:
Sirius Real Estate Limited ((GB:SRE)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Sirius Real Estate delivered a predominantly positive earnings call, highlighted by strong rent roll, rental income, EBITDA, FFO and dividend growth. Stable NAV, expansion in defense and self-storage, and attractive value-add returns outweighed concerns over higher finance costs, a first-half revaluation loss, fragile pricing growth and continued economic uncertainty.

Strong Rent Roll and FFO Growth

Sirius reported an 11.3% increase in total annualized rent roll. FFO rose 12% from just under EUR 65 million to more than EUR 72 million, while FFO per share increased 6.5% to EUR 0.0458.

Dividend Raised for 26th Consecutive Payment

The interim dividend increased 5.4% to EUR 0.0335 per share and is payable in January. Management said the dividend remains very well covered, marking the company’s 26th consecutive dividend payment.

Rental Income and EBITDA Expansion

First-half rental income rose 17% to EUR 131.8 million, while net operating income increased 19%. EBITDA climbed 21% to EUR 91.1 million, showing the benefits of operating leverage as the portfolio expands.

Portfolio Scale and Ownership

Sirius now operates more than EUR 3 billion of property, with 90% wholly owned. Its portfolio includes more than 160 sites and nearly 2,000 commercial buildings across 76 U.K. sites, 80 German sites and seven Titanium joint venture sites.

German Like-for-Like Growth

German rent roll increased from just over EUR 150 million to more than EUR 175 million. Like-for-like growth reached 5.1%, supported by a 1% occupancy increase and an almost 4% rise in rent per square meter.

U.K. Like-for-Like Growth

U.K. like-for-like rental growth was 5.2%, driven by a 1.3% increase in occupancy and a 3.8% price rise. U.K. move-ins also increased sharply, climbing 46.9% during the period.

Acquisitions Support Portfolio Growth

Sirius completed EUR 150 million of acquisitions, including defense-related assets in Kiel and Fulda. Investment properties increased by EUR 151 million, while management said EUR 75 million of acquisition capacity remains available in the current financial year.

Defense Portfolio Expands

The defense portfolio has grown to just over EUR 200 million following acquisitions in Munich, Bedford and elsewhere. Management sees an opportunity to expand the portfolio toward approximately EUR 500 million over time.

Defense Tenants Offer Growth Potential

The Kiel asset is occupied by a manufacturer of electronics for tanks and armored vehicles, while the Fulda site produces ballistic helmets and body armor. Management said defense tenants prioritize production capacity and speed, creating opportunities for additional space and tenant-funded expansion.

Self-Storage Revenues Increase

Smartspace self-storage operates in more than 30 German locations, serving over 4,000 customers, with four additional U.K. sites. Self-storage revenue rose more than 13%, and management sees a path to more than doubling the business.

Self-Storage Development Pipeline

Sirius is close to completing its first dedicated Berlin self-storage store and plans conversions in Coalville, Luton and Morden. It also intends to build a store in Potsdam, while the Gartenfeld development is being built near roughly 6,000 new homes.

Value-Add CapEx Produces High Returns

Over three years, Sirius developed 284,000 square meters with EUR 33.8 million of investment, adding EUR 13.9 million of annual rental income. That represents a 41% return on investment, while first-half CapEx totaled EUR 33.4 million, including EUR 11 million of value-add spending.

Large Value-Add Opportunity Remains

About 70% of the portfolio, worth EUR 1.697 billion, is classified as value-add, compared with EUR 650 million in mature assets. In Germany, 307,000 square meters of vacant space could receive CapEx to improve occupancy and generate additional value.

Value-Add Assets Have Further Upside

Value-add properties carry an 82% occupancy rate and a 7.8% gross yield, compared with 95% occupancy for mature properties. Moving assets toward mature status can reduce service charge losses and lift achieved rents from EUR 7.58 to EUR 8.87 per square meter.

New-Build Projects Target Strong Returns

The Gartenfeld self-storage development is expected to generate returns above 20%. Sirius has also invested in 72 garage self-storage units in Hanover, with 15 sold, and is spending about EUR 5 million on a Dresden project expected to deliver an internal rate of return above 20%.

Service Charge Recovery Improves

Service charge irrecoverables fell to 12.8% from 13.9% a year earlier. The improvement came despite the portfolio expanding by around 20% over the past 18 months.

Balance Sheet and NAV Remain Stable

Cash stood at EUR 99 million, including EUR 35 million of tenant deposits, while bank loans totaled EUR 1.25 billion. Adjusted NAV was EUR 1.2429 per share and EPRA NAV was just under EUR 1.22 per share, both described as relatively stable.

Recycling Creates Acquisition Capacity

The company continues to recycle capital through potential disposals of subscale U.K. assets and Pfungstadt in Germany. Management considers annual recycling of EUR 50 million to EUR 75 million realistic, with additional disposals potentially increasing acquisition capacity.

Technology Supports Self-Storage Growth

Sirius has completed a digital and AI-supported platform for self-storage, covering contracting, pricing, marketing and sales integration. It is also upgrading core customer relationship systems, particularly in Germany, with implementation costs described as one-off and immaterial to reported figures.

U.K. Market Reopens for Investment

Management said the U.K. market is now more stable and open to investment in new sites. Sirius is considering light industrial parks with defense potential and self-storage opportunities, while favoring conversions and new builds over single-site self-storage purchases.

Long-Term FFO Ambitions Maintained

Sirius reiterated its immediate ambition to reach EUR 150 million of FFO and its longer-term goal of exceeding that figure to reach EUR 175 million. Management said the longer-term target already reflects refinancing costs based on assumed interest rates of approximately 5.5% to 5.7%.

Trading Remains in Line With Expectations

Management said the company is trading in line with expectations and viewed the second half with a high degree of confidence. Organic growth also typically gains momentum later in the financial year.

Finance Costs Rise Sharply

Net finance expense increased to EUR 17.3 million from EUR 9.4 million following the refinancing of the June 2026 bond. Management said higher interest costs reduced revenue growth of 17.9% to FFO growth of 12% and expects full-year net finance expense to be around EUR 40 million.

First-Half Revaluation Turns Negative

Sirius recorded a EUR 24 million negative revaluation in the first half. Management attributed the decline mainly to CapEx investment in Germany, saying the impact should reverse as those investments begin producing rental income.

Joint Venture Income Declines Slightly

Joint venture income fell modestly to EUR 3.6 million. The prior-year period benefited from a performance fee, while the joint venture also refinanced its debt at the beginning of the current period.

Underlying Pricing Growth Is Fragile

Management said German rent growth of about 3.8% to 4% is only slightly above inflation. In the U.K., similar growth was described as more fragile, with renewal pricing and stronger platform capabilities needed to stay ahead of inflation.

New Business Requires Pricing Discounts

In Germany, new tenants are entering at EUR 0.21 below the like-for-like rent per square meter, while move-out and move-in rates differ by EUR 0.08. In the U.K., new-business pricing was reduced by 20% to support volume, helping move-ins rise 46.9% while occupancy increased 1.3%.

Tenant Turnover Delays Cash Flow

The first half typically brings higher levels of move-ins and move-outs. Some larger German spaces had been relet after CapEx but were not yet occupied, meaning rental cash flows had not started and short-term valuation pressure remained.

Operating Conditions Remain Challenging

Businesses in the U.K. continue to face cost pressure and bureaucracy, while German companies are dealing with utility prices around 300% above pre-war levels. Sirius is also discounting new-business pricing to attract sufficient tenant demand.

Political and Economic Uncertainty Persists

The company continues to operate against a backdrop of political and economic uncertainty. Key risks include possible instability around German local elections, changing interest rates and refinancing costs, and uncertainty over winter energy consumption.

Pfungstadt Sale Faces Delay

The buyer of the EUR 30 million Pfungstadt asset could not complete the transaction on the originally expected date because of a delayed sale elsewhere in its portfolio. Sirius therefore carried higher debt for longer, although the renegotiated terms included compensation and an interest penalty.

Near-Term Capital Raising Is Unlikely

Management said Sirius is not planning to raise capital in the near term. Instead, it intends to rely on asset recycling to fund potential acquisitions in the U.K.

CapEx Deployment Will Remain Controlled

Sirius is deliberately phasing its CapEx program rather than investing in all vacant space at once. Management said accelerating the program would move the company higher up the risk curve, making execution more demanding.

Refinancing Could Create a Future Headwind

The EUR 175 million FFO ambition includes roughly EUR 11 million of additional refinancing costs. This reflects assumed rates of 5.5% to 5.7% and the possibility that refinancing conditions may be less favorable than in the past.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management said EUR 150 million of FFO could be within reach this year, with EUR 175 million the longer-term ambition, while full-year net finance expense is expected to be around EUR 40 million. Sirius expects debt of EUR 1.25 billion to EUR 1.3 billion, annual recycling of EUR 50 million to EUR 75 million, and EUR 75 million of acquisition firepower in the current year.

The company also expects to expand its defense portfolio toward EUR 500 million and more than double self-storage revenue to above EUR 16 million. Around one-third of FFO is reinvested in CapEx, new-build projects are expected to generate returns above 20%, and management said it remains confident about the second half while trading in line with expectations.

Sirius Real Estate’s earnings call presented a company combining strong operating growth with disciplined capital allocation and substantial value-add potential. Higher financing costs, cautious pricing, valuation pressure and uncertain economic conditions remain important risks, but management’s confidence and expansion opportunities kept the overall message positive.

The call suggests Sirius is progressing toward its FFO goals while broadening its exposure to defense, self-storage and redevelopment. Investors will likely focus on whether pricing power improves, CapEx converts into occupancy and rental income, and recycling can fund growth without weakening the balance sheet.

data.title: Serko Earnings Call Highlights Growth and AI Investment
data.description:
Serko Ltd. ((NZ:SKO)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Serko’s earnings call struck a strongly positive tone, with accelerating Booking.com for Business growth, improving margins, positive free cash flow and a debt-free balance sheet. Serko.ai’s open-beta launch added to the optimism, although GetThere declines, early-stage AI investment, weak U.S. corporate segment conversion and second-half cash-flow seasonality remain important risks.

Strong First-Half Financial Performance

Serko reported a 17% increase in total income to $72.3 million, while total spend rose 12% to $66.4 million. EBITDAFI climbed 37% to $8.4 million, the net loss narrowed 91% to $0.9 million, and free cash flow nearly tripled from $3 million to $8.9 million.

Booking.com for Business Sets Records

Booking.com for Business delivered a record first half, with active customers up 38% to 363,000 and completed room nights rising 47% to 3 million. Revenue increased 33% to $47.9 million, supported by customer acquisition, product improvements, transfers from Booking.com’s core product and marketing demand.

Momentum Accelerates

Completed room nights rose 13% from the first quarter to the second, compared with 2% in the same period last year. Active customers grew 12% quarter-on-quarter, ahead of the 9% increase a year earlier, as earlier product upgrades lifted activity to a higher base.

Multi-Year Expansion Continues

Since the first half of FY’24, Booking.com for Business active customers have increased 106%, completed room nights have risen 128%, and revenue has grown 116%. Completed room nights have increased in every half since the first half of FY’25, showing sustained expansion rather than a one-off increase.

Operating Leverage Improves

Serko’s product and technology spending on Booking.com for Business fell from 39% of revenue in the first half of FY’24 to 19% in the latest half. Management said the change shows that each additional dollar of revenue now requires less investment to deliver.

Gross Margins Expand

Gross margin reached 90%, reinforcing the economics of Serko’s platform model. Over the past 4.5 years, revenue increased 282% while cost of sales rose 38%, and cost of sales was broadly flat across the last three halves even as revenue rose 17% versus the first half of FY’26.

Core Business Generates Cash

The established Zeno and Booking.com for Business operations generated enough cash to cover overheads and support substantial free cash flow. The core business produced $26.8 million of cash flow in the first half, despite $3.9 million of GetThere outflows and $14 million invested in Serko.ai.

Debt-Free Balance Sheet

Serko ended the half with about $63 million in cash and no debt, later reporting cash and deposits of $62 million. Management described the balance sheet as clean, giving the company resilience and flexibility as it invests in new products.

Australasia Delivers Positive Growth

Australasia travel revenue increased 5% to $14 million, while booking volumes remained broadly steady at 2.2 million. Average revenue per booking rose 12% to $6.23, mainly reflecting the stronger Australian dollar.

Serko.ai Enters Open Beta

Serko released Serko.ai into open beta in the United States in mid-October, following a closed beta that ran from May to September. The product allows travelers to plan, book, change or cancel trips in one conversation, while companies can set policy guardrails and monitor actual spending in real time.

Early AI Engagement Encourages

The open beta initially invited 800 people from the waitlist, and management said users were returning for multiple conversations while the first trips were being booked. Marketing activity has expanded to increase usage and gather more feedback over the coming months.

Large U.S. Small-Business Opportunity

Serko is starting with small teams and companies before moving toward larger businesses. Management estimates that U.S. small and medium-sized companies with up to 500 employees spend about $76 billion annually on travel, rising to roughly $84 billion when microbusinesses are included.

Corporate Segment Testing Advances

Serko has signed five U.S. corporate customers through its corporate segments initiative and said the testing has confirmed a clear market need. Interest remains broad across industries, while the program continues as a low-cost test-and-learn effort.

Efficiency Offsets New Investment

Total spend rose $7.2 million, or 12%, including $14.5 million invested in Serko.ai. That increase was partly offset by $7.3 million of efficiency and effectiveness gains elsewhere, including cost reductions in Zeno and ongoing technical and commercial improvements.

Reported Loss Drivers Improve

Amortization and depreciation fell $1.9 million to $7.5 million, asset impairments and disposals declined $1.4 million to $0.7 million, and foreign exchange losses dropped $2.8 million to $0.9 million. Amortization decreased 27% to $6.1 million, while intangible assets fell from $35 million in March 2023 to $17.1 million.

Guidance Raised on Income

Serko lifted its FY’27 total income guidance to $135 million-$141 million, from the previous range of $128 million-$134 million. Management continues to expect total spend toward the middle of its $132 million-$140 million guidance range.

Demand Remains Resilient

Management described business travel demand in key markets as robust despite geopolitical uncertainty and difficult macroeconomic conditions. First-half momentum had carried into the second half, supporting expectations for continued underlying growth on a seasonally adjusted basis.

GetThere U.S. Bookings Decline

GetThere’s U.S. online bookings fell 15% year-on-year to 1.5 million, although the decline was smaller than expected. Bookings increased 9% from the second half of the prior year, but management remains focused on slowing the decline and using AI to support growth.

Corporate Segment Adoption Is Limited

Although Serko has signed five U.S. corporate customers and continues to see interest, adoption has so far been limited. Converting sign-ups into meaningful booking volume is taking longer than expected, so the company is concentrating on increasing activity within each customer.

No Near-Term Corporate Revenue

Management does not expect meaningful revenue from the U.S. corporate segments initiative during FY’27. The comments underline that the program remains focused on validating demand and improving customer activity rather than contributing materially to current-year results.

Supply Issues Hinder Conversion

Some corporate customers have faced supply-related obstacles, including difficulty fulfilling bookings that require specific accommodation features or locations with limited availability. Serko is working with Booking.com to identify which of these issues can be resolved.

Revenue Per Room Night Falls

Booking.com’s average commission per room night was broadly stable but fell 1%, while Serko’s average revenue per completed room night declined 12% as more volume moved into lower incremental tiers. Revenue growth still outweighed that pressure because completed room nights increased 47%.

Australasia Service Revenue Declines

Australasia service revenue was lower after the completion of NDC project work in FY’26. Booking volumes remained broadly steady at 2.2 million, showing that the decline reflected the end of project revenue rather than weaker transaction activity.

Second-Half Cash Flow Will Be Lower

FY’27 free cash flow is expected to remain positive but below the $8.9 million recorded in the first half. Management attributed the expected reduction to normal revenue seasonality, payment timing and continued investment in Serko.ai.

Serko.ai Remains at an Early Stage

Management emphasized that Serko.ai is still in a testing and learning phase, with no meaningful demand yet observed from external AI agents. The company also has not settled on a long-term commercial model, leaving the product’s eventual economics uncertain.

AI Investment Increases

Serko expects to spend somewhat more on Serko.ai in the second half than in the first half. Serko.ai represented $14.5 million of total spend and about $14 million of related cash outflows during the first half.

GetThere Faces Customer Churn

GetThere experienced customer departures following its acquisition, and management is now seeing a modest level of churn within the existing base. Some customers that had signaled plans to leave have continued to move meaningful volumes away from the platform.

Seasonality and Uncertainty Persist

The second half is normally weaker than the first because of customer receipt and supplier payment timing. Management also pointed to economic and geopolitical volatility, including possible effects from the conflict in the Middle East on business travel demand.

Net Loss Remains Slightly Negative

Despite an $8.6 million year-on-year improvement, Serko reported a net loss after tax of $0.9 million for the first half. The result shows that strong operating progress has not yet translated into a fully profitable bottom line.

FY’27 Outlook

Serko now expects FY’27 total income of $135 million-$141 million, while total spend is expected near the middle of the $132 million-$140 million range. Free cash flow should remain positive but below the first-half level, with the outlook implying second-half completed room-nights growth above 50% and activity per business around 8.5 to 9.

Meaningful revenue from the U.S. corporate segments initiative is not expected this year, while economic and geopolitical uncertainty could affect travel demand. The guidance reflects strong Booking.com for Business momentum but also allows for seasonal cash-flow pressure and heavier Serko.ai investment.

Overall, Serko’s earnings call showed a company gaining scale, improving efficiency and strengthening its financial position. Booking.com for Business is the main growth engine, while Serko.ai offers longer-term potential; however, GetThere’s decline, limited corporate-segment conversion and continued AI spending remain key issues for investors to monitor.
